analyst_view.overall: Eibar (7th, 24 pts from 14) host Burgos (5th, 27 pts from 15) at Ipurua in a meeting of two promotion play-off hopefuls. Eibar's form has dipped (last five DLDDL), most recently a 2-1 defeat at Girona where Mada scored a penalty and both Jon Magunazelaia and Aleix Garrido needed treatment before being substituted later on. Burgos come in after a 1-0 home win over Albacete (an own goal from a Javi Llabres cross) in which they picked up four yellow cards. Flashscore lists defenders Bernat Juan and Imanol Garcia de Albeniz and midfielder Elijah Gift as injured for Eibar; I found no confirmed absences for Burgos, no referee yet, and news for this match was thin. The numbers already count both sides' recent form and the six past meetings, so this view stays close to them.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals, pulled down a little by six tight past meetings. Eibar's games this season average close to 3 goals (23 for, 17 against in 14) and Burgos' about 2.5, but both sides' recent scoring is already in the momentum adjustment, and the Eibar injuries I found are defenders and a squad midfielder rather than their scorers (Guruzeta and Ivan Gil have 4 each). Nothing new points either way, so I stay at 1.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. Burgos win a lot of them lately (37 in their last six) and press down the left through Llabres, which drove most of their chances against Albacete; the numbers already add about 9% to Burgos' side for that. With no lineup news that changes the wide play, I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. Burgos are among the more booked sides (40 yellows in 15 games, four against Albacete) and Eibar have two reds this season; both teams' recent card counts are already in the numbers. The referee has not been named yet, so there is nothing to add for him; I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.7 shots. Both teams have been shooting more than usual over the last six games (Eibar 96, Burgos 89), and the numbers already raise both sides for it. Eibar play a Copa del Rey tie at Sant Andreu on 2 December, after this match, so no rotation is expected here; I stay at 25.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. Burgos have put 30 on target in their last six and Eibar have conceded 34, which the numbers already count with about +12% on Burgos' side. With Eibar's main forwards fit as far as I could find, I stay at 8.1.
